page: OVHcloud c3-16 is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 8 dedicated physical cores running on AMD EPYC processors at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The virtualization environment runs on KVM without hyper-threading, providing a strictly 1:1 mapping of 8 vCPUs across 8 physical cores. Memory capacity is provisioned at 16.0 GB total, delivering a compute-centric 2.0 GB per core. The hardware architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by standard hardware cryptographic extensions including AES and SHA-NI.

Storage and networking configurations include an integrated 200 GB local NVMe SSD, eliminating external network-storage latency for local scratch and persistent application tasks. Network performance is anchored by a baseline throughput of 1 Gbps. The instance includes 0 complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not feature dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate robust single-thread compute capabilities, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core execution (3078.28) and Geekbench text processing (2627.0). Multi-core processing aligns solidly within the middle tier, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 20439.77 and Geekbench multi-core score of 9537.0. Memory throughput reaches 148.76 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 76.63 GB/sec for large block writes. In targeted CPU inference tests, text generation using small 135M language models placed in the top 25% at 275.19 tokens per second, while larger 7B model execution delivered average performance at 20.24 tokens per second.

The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio makes the instance cost-efficient for CPU-bound pipelines that do not demand extensive in-memory structures. It is well matched for software compilation, batch processing, CI/CD runners, containerized web microservices, and localized analytical parsing workloads.
description: OVHcloud c3-16 is a compute-optimized x86_64 cloud server powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz. Configured without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers 8 dedicated physical cores across 8 vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a focused 1:2 RAM-to-core allocation. Storage is provided via a bundled 200 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by a 1 Gbps network baseline. Synthetic testing displays top-quartile execution in stress-ng single-core execution and text processing, supported by average multi-core marks in Geekbench and PassMark. With no GPU hardware attached, this server is suitable for CPU-bound workloads requiring consistent execution without hyper-thread contention, including software build pipelines, batch data transforms, microservices, and general compute-driven operations.
